CreateActivity.name: CreateActivity
CreateActivity.doc: Creates an activity. An activity is a task that you write in any programming language and host on any machine that has access to Step Functions. Activities must poll Step Functions using the GetActivityTask API action and respond using SendTask* API actions. This function lets Step Functions know the existence of your activity and returns an identifier for use in a state machine and when polling…

CreateStateMachine.name: CreateStateMachine
CreateStateMachine.doc: Creates a state machine. A state machine consists of a collection of states that can do work (Task states), determine to which states to transition next (Choice states), stop an execution with an error (Fail states), and so on. State machines are specified using a JSON-based, structured language. For more information, see Amazon States Language in the Step Functions User Guide. If you set the…

CreateStateMachineAlias.name: CreateStateMachineAlias
CreateStateMachineAlias.doc: Creates an alias for a state machine that points to one or two versions of the same state machine. You can set your application to call StartExecution with an alias and update the version the alias uses without changing the client's code. You can also map an alias to split StartExecution requests between two versions of a state machine. To do this, add a second RoutingConfig object in the…

DeleteStateMachine.name: DeleteStateMachine
DeleteStateMachine.doc: Deletes a state machine. This is an asynchronous operation. It sets the state machine's status to DELETING and begins the deletion process. A state machine is deleted only when all its executions are completed. On the next state transition, the state machine's executions are terminated. A qualified state machine ARN can either refer to a Distributed Map state defined within a state machine, a…

DeleteStateMachineAlias.name: DeleteStateMachineAlias
DeleteStateMachineAlias.doc: Deletes a state machine alias. After you delete a state machine alias, you can't use it to start executions. When you delete a state machine alias, Step Functions doesn't delete the state machine versions that alias references. Related operations: CreateStateMachineAlias DescribeStateMachineAlias ListStateMachineAliases UpdateStateMachineAlias

DeleteStateMachineVersion.name: DeleteStateMachineVersion
DeleteStateMachineVersion.doc: Deletes a state machine version. After you delete a version, you can't call StartExecution using that version's ARN or use the version with a state machine alias. Deleting a state machine version won't terminate its in-progress executions. You can't delete a state machine version currently referenced by one or more aliases. Before you delete a version, you must either delete the aliases or update…

DescribeActivity.name: DescribeActivity
DescribeActivity.doc: Describes an activity. This operation is eventually consistent. The results are best effort and may not reflect very recent updates and changes.

DescribeExecution.name: DescribeExecution
DescribeExecution.doc: Provides information about a state machine execution, such as the state machine associated with the execution, the execution input and output, and relevant execution metadata. If you've redriven an execution, you can use this API action to return information about the redrives of that execution. In addition, you can use this API action to return the Map Run Amazon Resource Name (ARN) if the…

DescribeMapRun.name: DescribeMapRun
DescribeMapRun.doc: Provides information about a Map Run's configuration, progress, and results. If you've redriven a Map Run, this API action also returns information about the redrives of that Map Run. For more information, see Examining Map Run in the Step Functions Developer Guide.

DescribeStateMachine.name: DescribeStateMachine
DescribeStateMachine.doc: Provides information about a state machine's definition, its IAM role Amazon Resource Name (ARN), and configuration. A qualified state machine ARN can either refer to a Distributed Map state defined within a state machine, a version ARN, or an alias ARN. The following are some examples of qualified and unqualified state machine ARNs: The following qualified state machine ARN refers to a…

DescribeStateMachineAlias.name: DescribeStateMachineAlias
DescribeStateMachineAlias.doc: Returns details about a state machine alias. Related operations: CreateStateMachineAlias ListStateMachineAliases UpdateStateMachineAlias DeleteStateMachineAlias

DescribeStateMachineForExecution.name: DescribeStateMachineForExecution
DescribeStateMachineForExecution.doc: Provides information about a state machine's definition, its execution role ARN, and configuration. If a Map Run dispatched the execution, this action returns the Map Run Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the response. The state machine returned is the state machine associated with the Map Run. This operation is eventually consistent. The results are best effort and may not reflect very recent…

GetActivityTask.name: GetActivityTask
GetActivityTask.doc: Used by workers to retrieve a task (with the specified activity ARN) which has been scheduled for execution by a running state machine. This initiates a long poll, where the service holds the HTTP connection open and responds as soon as a task becomes available (i.e. an execution of a task of this type is needed.) The maximum time the service holds on to the request before responding is 60…

GetExecutionHistory.name: GetExecutionHistory
GetExecutionHistory.doc: Returns the history of the specified execution as a list of events. By default, the results are returned in ascending order of the timeStamp of the events. Use the reverseOrder parameter to get the latest events first. If nextToken is returned, there are more results available. The value of nextToken is a unique pagination token for each page. Make the call again using the returned token to…

ListActivities.name: ListActivities
ListActivities.doc: Lists the existing activities. If nextToken is returned, there are more results available. The value of nextToken is a unique pagination token for each page. Make the call again using the returned token to retrieve the next page. Keep all other arguments unchanged. Each pagination token expires after 24 hours. Using an expired pagination token will return an HTTP 400 InvalidToken error. This…

ListExecutions.name: ListExecutions
ListExecutions.doc: Lists all executions of a state machine or a Map Run. You can list all executions related to a state machine by specifying a state machine Amazon Resource Name (ARN), or those related to a Map Run by specifying a Map Run ARN. Using this API action, you can also list all redriven executions. You can also provide a state machine alias ARN or version ARN to list the executions associated with a…

ListMapRuns.name: ListMapRuns
ListMapRuns.doc: Lists all Map Runs that were started by a given state machine execution. Use this API action to obtain Map Run ARNs, and then call DescribeMapRun to obtain more information, if needed.

ListStateMachineAliases.name: ListStateMachineAliases
ListStateMachineAliases.doc: Lists aliases for a specified state machine ARN. Results are sorted by time, with the most recently created aliases listed first. To list aliases that reference a state machine version, you can specify the version ARN in the stateMachineArn parameter. If nextToken is returned, there are more results available. The value of nextToken is a unique pagination token for each page. Make the call again…

ListStateMachines.name: ListStateMachines
ListStateMachines.doc: Lists the existing state machines. If nextToken is returned, there are more results available. The value of nextToken is a unique pagination token for each page. Make the call again using the returned token to retrieve the next page. Keep all other arguments unchanged. Each pagination token expires after 24 hours. Using an expired pagination token will return an HTTP 400 InvalidToken error. This…

ListStateMachineVersions.name: ListStateMachineVersions
ListStateMachineVersions.doc: Lists versions for the specified state machine Amazon Resource Name (ARN). The results are sorted in descending order of the version creation time. If nextToken is returned, there are more results available. The value of nextToken is a unique pagination token for each page. Make the call again using the returned token to retrieve the next page. Keep all other arguments unchanged. Each pagination…

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.doc: List tags for a given resource. Tags may only contain Unicode letters, digits, white space, or these symbols: _ . : / = + - @.

PublishStateMachineVersion.name: PublishStateMachineVersion
PublishStateMachineVersion.doc: Creates a version from the current revision of a state machine. Use versions to create immutable snapshots of your state machine. You can start executions from versions either directly or with an alias. To create an alias, use CreateStateMachineAlias. You can publish up to 1000 versions for each state machine. You must manually delete unused versions using the DeleteStateMachineVersion API…

RedriveExecution.name: RedriveExecution
RedriveExecution.doc: Restarts unsuccessful executions of Standard workflows that didn't complete successfully in the last 14 days. These include failed, aborted, or timed out executions. When you redrive an execution, it continues the failed execution from the unsuccessful step and uses the same input. Step Functions preserves the results and execution history of the successful steps, and doesn't rerun these steps…

SendTaskFailure.name: SendTaskFailure
SendTaskFailure.doc: Used by activity workers, Task states using the callback pattern, and optionally Task states using the job run pattern to report that the task identified by the taskToken failed. For an execution with encryption enabled, Step Functions will encrypt the error and cause fields using the KMS key for the execution role. A caller can mark a task as fail without using any KMS permissions in the…

SendTaskHeartbeat.name: SendTaskHeartbeat
SendTaskHeartbeat.doc: Used by activity workers and Task states using the callback pattern, and optionally Task states using the job run pattern to report to Step Functions that the task represented by the specified taskToken is still making progress. This action resets the Heartbeat clock. The Heartbeat threshold is specified in the state machine's Amazon States Language definition (HeartbeatSeconds). This action does…

SendTaskSuccess.name: SendTaskSuccess
SendTaskSuccess.doc: Used by activity workers, Task states using the callback pattern, and optionally Task states using the job run pattern to report that the task identified by the taskToken completed successfully.

StartExecution.name: StartExecution
StartExecution.doc: Starts a state machine execution. A qualified state machine ARN can either refer to a Distributed Map state defined within a state machine, a version ARN, or an alias ARN. The following are some examples of qualified and unqualified state machine ARNs: The following qualified state machine ARN refers to a Distributed Map state with a label mapStateLabel in a state machine named myStateMachine.…

StartSyncExecution.name: StartSyncExecution
StartSyncExecution.doc: Starts a Synchronous Express state machine execution. StartSyncExecution is not available for STANDARD workflows. StartSyncExecution will return a 200 OK response, even if your execution fails, because the status code in the API response doesn't reflect function errors. Error codes are reserved for errors that prevent your execution from running, such as permissions errors, limit errors, or…

StopExecution.name: StopExecution
StopExecution.doc: Stops an execution. This API action is not supported by EXPRESS state machines. For an execution with encryption enabled, Step Functions will encrypt the error and cause fields using the KMS key for the execution role. A caller can stop an execution without using any KMS permissions in the execution role if the caller provides a null value for both error and cause fields because no data needs to…

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.doc: Add a tag to a Step Functions resource. An array of key-value pairs. For more information, see Using Cost Allocation Tags in the Amazon Web Services Billing and Cost Management User Guide, and Controlling Access Using IAM Tags. Tags may only contain Unicode letters, digits, white space, or these symbols: _ . : / = + - @.

TestState.name: TestState
TestState.doc: Accepts the definition of a single state and executes it. You can test a state without creating a state machine or updating an existing state machine. Using this API, you can test the following: A state's input and output processing data flow An Amazon Web Services service integration request and response An HTTP Task request and response You can call this API on only one state at a time. The…

UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.doc: Remove a tag from a Step Functions resource

UpdateMapRun.name: UpdateMapRun
UpdateMapRun.doc: Updates an in-progress Map Run's configuration to include changes to the settings that control maximum concurrency and Map Run failure.

UpdateStateMachine.name: UpdateStateMachine
UpdateStateMachine.doc: Updates an existing state machine by modifying its definition, roleArn, loggingConfiguration, or EncryptionConfiguration. Running executions will continue to use the previous definition and roleArn. You must include at least one of definition or roleArn or you will receive a MissingRequiredParameter error. A qualified state machine ARN refers to a Distributed Map state defined within a state…

UpdateStateMachineAlias.name: UpdateStateMachineAlias
UpdateStateMachineAlias.doc: Updates the configuration of an existing state machine alias by modifying its description or routingConfiguration. You must specify at least one of the description or routingConfiguration parameters to update a state machine alias. UpdateStateMachineAlias is an idempotent API. Step Functions bases the idempotency check on the stateMachineAliasArn, description, and routingConfiguration parameters.…

ValidateStateMachineDefinition.name: ValidateStateMachineDefinition
ValidateStateMachineDefinition.doc: Validates the syntax of a state machine definition specified in Amazon States Language (ASL), a JSON-based, structured language. You can validate that a state machine definition is correct without creating a state machine resource. Suggested uses for ValidateStateMachineDefinition: Integrate automated checks into your code review or Continuous Integration (CI) process to check state machine…

cause.doc: A more detailed explanation of the cause of the failure.

heartbeatInSeconds.doc: The maximum allowed duration between two heartbeats for the activity task.

AssignedVariablesDetails.doc: Provides details about assigned variables in an execution history event.

billedMemoryUsedInMB.doc: Billed memory consumption of your workflow, in MB.

billedDurationInMilliseconds.doc: Billed duration of your workflow, in milliseconds.

BillingDetails.doc: An object that describes workflow billing details.

included.doc: Indicates whether input or output was included in the response. Always true for API calls.

CloudWatchEventsExecutionDataDetails.doc: Provides details about execution input or output.

logGroupArn.doc: The ARN of the the CloudWatch log group to which you want your logs emitted to. The ARN must end with :*

name.doc: The name of the activity to create. This name must be unique for your Amazon Web Services account and region for 90 days. For more information, see Limits Related to State Machine Executions in the Step Functions Developer Guide. A name must not contain: white space brackets < > { } [ ] wildcard characters ? * special characters " # % \ ^ | ~ ` $ & , ; : / control characters (U+0000-001F,…

tags.doc: The list of tags to add to a resource. An array of key-value pairs. For more information, see Using Cost Allocation Tags in the Amazon Web Services Billing and Cost Management User Guide, and Controlling Access Using IAM Tags. Tags may only contain Unicode letters, digits, white space, or these symbols: _ . : / = + - @.

activityArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the created activity.

creationDate.doc: The date the activity is created.

description.doc: A description for the state machine alias.

name.doc: The name of the state machine alias. To avoid conflict with version ARNs, don't use an integer in the name of the alias.

routingConfiguration.doc: The routing configuration of a state machine alias. The routing configuration shifts execution traffic between two state machine versions. routingConfiguration contains an array of RoutingConfig objects that specify up to two state machine versions. Step Functions then randomly choses which version to run an execution with based on the weight assigned to each RoutingConfig.

stateMachineAliasArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the created state machine alias.

creationDate.doc: The date the state machine alias was created.

name.doc: The name of the state machine. A name must not contain: white space brackets < > { } [ ] wildcard characters ? * special characters " # % \ ^ | ~ ` $ & , ; : / control characters (U+0000-001F, U+007F-009F, U+FFFE-FFFF) surrogates (U+D800-DFFF) invalid characters ( U+10FFFF) To enable logging with CloudWatch Logs, the name should only contain 0-9, A-Z, a-z, - and _.

definition.doc: The Amazon States Language definition of the state machine. See Amazon States Language.

roleArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role to use for this state machine.

type.doc: Determines whether a Standard or Express state machine is created. The default is STANDARD. You cannot update the type of a state machine once it has been created.

loggingConfiguration.doc: Defines what execution history events are logged and where they are logged. By default, the level is set to OFF. For more information see Log Levels in the Step Functions User Guide.

tags.doc: Tags to be added when creating a state machine. An array of key-value pairs. For more information, see Using Cost Allocation Tags in the Amazon Web Services Billing and Cost Management User Guide, and Controlling Access Using IAM Tags. Tags may only contain Unicode letters, digits, white space, or these symbols: _ . : / = + - @.

tracingConfiguration.doc: Selects whether X-Ray tracing is enabled.

publish.doc: Set to true to publish the first version of the state machine during creation. The default is false.

versionDescription.doc: Sets description about the state machine version. You can only set the description if the publish parameter is set to true. Otherwise, if you set versionDescription, but publish to false, this API action throws ValidationException.

stateMachineArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the created state machine.

creationDate.doc: The date the state machine is created.

stateMachineVersionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the created state machine version. If you do not set the publish parameter to true, this field returns null value.

activityArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the activity to delete.

stateMachineAliasArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine alias to delete.

stateMachineArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine to delete.

stateMachineVersionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine version to delete.

name.doc: The name of the activity. status.doc: The current status of the execution.

startDate.doc: The date the execution is started.

stopDate.doc: If the execution ended, the date the execution stopped.

output.doc: The JSON output data of the execution. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding. This field is set only if the execution succeeds. If the execution fails, this field is null.

traceHeader.doc: The X-Ray trace header that was passed to the execution. For X-Ray traces, all Amazon Web Services services use the X-Amzn-Trace-Id header from the HTTP request. Using the header is the preferred mechanism to identify a trace. StartExecution and StartSyncExecution API operations can also use traceHeader from the body of the request payload. If both sources are provided, Step Functions will use…

mapRunArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a Map Run, which dispatched this execution.

error.doc: The error string if the state machine execution failed.

cause.doc: The cause string if the state machine execution failed.

stateMachineVersionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine version associated with the execution. The version ARN is a combination of state machine ARN and the version number separated by a colon (:). For example, stateMachineARN:1. If you start an execution from a StartExecution request without specifying a state machine version or alias ARN, Step Functions returns a null value.

stateMachineAliasArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine alias associated with the execution. The alias ARN is a combination of state machine ARN and the alias name separated by a colon (:). For example, stateMachineARN:PROD. If you start an execution from a StartExecution request with a state machine version ARN, this field will be null.

redriveCount.doc: The number of times you've redriven an execution. If you have not yet redriven an execution, the redriveCount is 0. This count is only updated if you successfully redrive an execution.

redriveDate.doc: The date the execution was last redriven. If you have not yet redriven an execution, the redriveDate is null. The redriveDate is unavailable if you redrive a Map Run that starts child workflow executions of type EXPRESS.

redriveStatus.doc: Indicates whether or not an execution can be redriven at a given point in time. For executions of type STANDARD, redriveStatus is NOT_REDRIVABLE if calling the RedriveExecution API action would return the ExecutionNotRedrivable error. For a Distributed Map that includes child workflows of type STANDARD, redriveStatus indicates whether or not the Map Run can redrive child workflow executions. For…

redriveStatusReason.doc: When redriveStatus is NOT_REDRIVABLE, redriveStatusReason specifies the reason why an execution cannot be redriven. For executions of type STANDARD, or for a Distributed Map that includes child workflows of type STANDARD, redriveStatusReason can include one of the following reasons: State machine is in DELETING status. Execution is RUNNING and cannot be redriven. Execution is SUCCEEDED and cannot…

mapRunArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a Map Run.
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a Map Run.

executionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the execution in which the Map Run was started.

status.doc: The current status of the Map Run.

stopDate.doc: The date when the Map Run was stopped.

maxConcurrency.doc: The maximum number of child workflow executions configured to run in parallel for the Map Run at the same time.

toleratedFailureCount.doc: The maximum number of failed child workflow executions before the Map Run fails.

StartExecution and StartSyncExecution API operations can also use traceHeader from the body of the request payload. If both sources are…

includedData.doc: If your state machine definition is encrypted with a KMS key, callers must have kms:Decrypt permission to decrypt the definition. Alternatively, you can call the API with includedData = METADATA_ONLY to get a successful response without the encrypted definition.

executionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the execution.

stateMachineArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the state machine.

startDate.doc: The date the execution is started.

stopDate.doc: If the execution has already ended, the date the execution stopped.

status.doc: The current status of the execution.

error.doc: The error code of the failure.

cause.doc: A more detailed explanation of the cause of the failure.

input.doc: The string that contains the JSON input data of the execution. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding.

output.doc: The JSON output data of the execution. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding. This field is set only if the execution succeeds. If the execution fails, this field is null.

traceHeader.doc: The X-Ray trace header that was passed to the execution. For X-Ray traces, all Amazon Web Services services use the X-Amzn-Trace-Id header from the HTTP request. Using the header is the preferred mechanism to identify a trace. StartExecution and StartSyncExecution API operations can also use traceHeader from the body of the request payload. If both sources are provided, Step Functions will use…

billingDetails.doc: An object that describes workflow billing details, including billed duration and memory use.

input.doc: The string that contains the JSON input data for the state. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding.

inputDetails.doc: Contains details about the input for an execution history event.

StateEnteredEventDetails.doc: Contains details about a state entered during an execution.

name.doc: The name of the state. A name must not contain: white space brackets < > { } [ ] wildcard characters ? * special characters " # % \ ^ | ~ ` $ & , ; : / control characters (U+0000-001F, U+007F-009F, U+FFFE-FFFF) surrogates (U+D800-DFFF) invalid characters ( U+10FFFF) To enable logging with CloudWatch Logs, the name should only contain 0-9, A-Z, a-z, - and _.

output.doc: The JSON output data of the state. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding.

outputDetails.doc: Contains details about the output of an execution history event.

assignedVariables.doc: Map of variable name and value as a serialized JSON representation.

assignedVariablesDetails.doc: Provides details about input or output in an execution history event.

StateExitedEventDetails.doc: Contains details about an exit from a state during an execution.

stateMachineAliasArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a state machine alias. The alias ARN is a combination of state machine ARN and the alias name separated by a colon (:). For example, stateMachineARN:PROD.

creationDate.doc: The creation date of a state machine alias.

StateMachineAliasListItem.doc: Contains details about a specific state machine alias.

stateMachineArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the state machine.

name.doc: The name of the state machine. A name must not contain: white space brackets < > { } [ ] wildcard characters ? * special characters " # % \ ^ | ~ ` $ & , ; : / control characters (U+0000-001F, U+007F-009F, U+FFFE-FFFF) surrogates (U+D800-DFFF) invalid characters ( U+10FFFF) To enable logging with CloudWatch Logs, the name should only contain 0-9, A-Z, a-z, - and _.

creationDate.doc: The date the state machine is created.

StateMachineListItem.doc: Contains details about the state machine.

stateMachineVersionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a state machine version. The version ARN is a combination of state machine ARN and the version number separated by a colon (:). For example, stateMachineARN:1.

creationDate.doc: The creation date of a state machine version.

StateMachineVersionListItem.doc: Contains details about a specific state machine version.

executionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the execution to stop.

error.doc: The error code of the failure.

cause.doc: A more detailed explanation of the cause of the failure.

stopDate.doc: The date the execution is stopped.

Tag.doc: Tags are key-value pairs that can be associated with Step Functions state machines and activities. An array of key-value pairs. For more information, see Using Cost Allocation Tags in the Amazon Web Services Billing and Cost Management User Guide, and Controlling Access Using IAM Tags. Tags may only contain Unicode letters, digits, white space, or these symbols: _ . : / = + - @.

resourceArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the Step Functions state machine or activity.

tags.doc: The list of tags to add to a resource. Tags may only contain Unicode letters, digits, white space, or these symbols: _ . : / = + - @.

roleArn.doc: The ARN of an IAM role that Step Functions assumes for the task. The role can allow cross-account access to resources.

TaskCredentials.doc: Contains details about the credentials that Step Functions uses for a task.

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

error.doc: The error code of the failure.

cause.doc: A more detailed explanation of the cause of the failure.

TaskFailedEventDetails.doc: Contains details about a task failure event.

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

region.doc: The region of the scheduled task

parameters.doc: The JSON data passed to the resource referenced in a task state. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding.

timeoutInSeconds.doc: The maximum allowed duration of the task.

heartbeatInSeconds.doc: The maximum allowed duration between two heartbeats for the task.

taskCredentials.doc: The credentials that Step Functions uses for the task.

TaskScheduledEventDetails.doc: Contains details about a task scheduled during an execution.

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

error.doc: The error code of the failure.

cause.doc: A more detailed explanation of the cause of the failure.

TaskStartFailedEventDetails.doc: Contains details about a task that failed to start during an execution.

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

TaskStartedEventDetails.doc: Contains details about the start of a task during an execution.

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

error.doc: The error code of the failure.

cause.doc: A more detailed explanation of the cause of the failure.

TaskSubmitFailedEventDetails.doc: Contains details about a task that failed to submit during an execution.

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

output.doc: The response from a resource when a task has started. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding.

outputDetails.doc: Contains details about the output of an execution history event.

TaskSubmittedEventDetails.doc: Contains details about a task submitted to a resource .

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

output.doc: The full JSON response from a resource when a task has succeeded. This response becomes the output of the related task. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding.

outputDetails.doc: Contains details about the output of an execution history event.

TaskSucceededEventDetails.doc: Contains details about the successful completion of a task state.

resourceType.doc: The service name of the resource in a task state.

resource.doc: The action of the resource called by a task state.

error.doc: The error code of the failure.

cause.doc: A more detailed explanation of the cause of the failure.

TaskTimedOutEventDetails.doc: Contains details about a resource timeout that occurred during an execution.

retrierRetryCount.doc: The number of retry attempts that have occurred for the state's Retry that applies to the mocked error.

errorCausedByState.doc: The name of the state from which an error originates when an error is mocked for a Map or Parallel state.

mapIterationFailureCount.doc: The number of Map state iterations that failed during the Map state invocation.

mapItemReaderData.doc: The data read by ItemReader in Distributed Map states as found in its original source.

TestStateConfiguration.doc: Contains configurations for the tested state.

definition.doc: The Amazon States Language (ASL) definition of the state or state machine.

roleArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the execution role with the required IAM permissions for the state.

input.doc: A string that contains the JSON input data for the state.

inspectionLevel.doc: Determines the values to return when a state is tested. You can specify one of the following types: INFO: Shows the final state output. By default, Step Functions sets inspectionLevel to INFO if you don't specify a level. DEBUG: Shows the final state output along with the input and output data processing result. TRACE: Shows the HTTP request and response for an HTTP Task. This level also shows…

revealSecrets.doc: Specifies whether or not to include secret information in the test result. For HTTP Tasks, a secret includes the data that an EventBridge connection adds to modify the HTTP request headers, query parameters, and body. Step Functions doesn't omit any information included in the state definition or the HTTP response. If you set revealSecrets to true, you must make sure that the IAM user that calls…

variables.doc: JSON object literal that sets variables used in the state under test. Object keys are the variable names and values are the variable values.

stateName.doc: Denotes the particular state within a state machine definition to be tested. If this field is specified, the definition must contain a fully-formed state machine definition.

mock.doc: Defines a mocked result or error for the state under test. A mock can only be specified for Task, Map, or Parallel states. If it is specified for another state type, an exception will be thrown.

context.doc: A JSON string representing a valid Context object for the state under test. This field may only be specified if a mock is specified in the same request.

stateConfiguration.doc: Contains configurations for the state under test.

output.doc: The JSON output data of the state. Length constraints apply to the payload size, and are expressed as bytes in UTF-8 encoding.

error.doc: The error returned when the execution of a state fails.

cause.doc: A detailed explanation of the cause for the error when the execution of a state fails.

inspectionData.doc: Returns additional details about the state's execution, including its input and output data processing flow, and HTTP request and response information. The inspectionLevel request parameter specifies which details are returned.

nextState.doc: The name of the next state to transition to. If you haven't defined a next state in your definition or if the execution of the state fails, this field doesn't contain a value.

status.doc: The execution status of the state.

enabled.doc: When set to true, X-Ray tracing is enabled.

TracingConfiguration.doc: Selects whether or not the state machine's X-Ray tracing is enabled. Default is false

resourceArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the Step Functions state machine or activity.

tagKeys.doc: The list of tags to remove from the resource.

mapRunArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a Map Run.

maxConcurrency.doc: The maximum number of child workflow executions that can be specified to run in parallel for the Map Run at the same time.

toleratedFailurePercentage.doc: The maximum percentage of failed items before the Map Run fails.

toleratedFailureCount.doc: The maximum number of failed items before the Map Run fails.

stateMachineAliasArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine alias.

description.doc: A description of the state machine alias.

routingConfiguration.doc: The routing configuration of the state machine alias. An array of RoutingConfig objects that specifies up to two state machine versions that the alias starts executions for.

updateDate.doc: The date and time the state machine alias was updated.

stateMachineArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the state machine.

definition.doc: The Amazon States Language definition of the state machine. See Amazon States Language.

roleArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role of the state machine.

loggingConfiguration.doc: Use the LoggingConfiguration data type to set CloudWatch Logs options.

tracingConfiguration.doc: Selects whether X-Ray tracing is enabled.

publish.doc: Specifies whether the state machine version is published. The default is false. To publish a version after updating the state machine, set publish to true.

versionDescription.doc: An optional description of the state machine version to publish. You can only specify the versionDescription parameter if you've set publish to true.

updateDate.doc: The date and time the state machine was updated.

revisionId.doc: The revision identifier for the updated state machine.

stateMachineVersionArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the published state machine version. If the publish parameter isn't set to true, this field returns null.

severity.doc: A value of ERROR means that you cannot create or update a state machine with this definition. WARNING level diagnostics alert you to potential issues, but they will not prevent you from creating or updating your state machine.

location.doc: Location of the issue in the state machine, if available. For errors specific to a field, the location could be in the format: /States/<StateName>/<FieldName>, for example: /States/FailState/ErrorPath.

ValidateStateMachineDefinitionDiagnostic.doc: Describes potential issues found during state machine validation. Rather than raise an exception, validation will return a list of diagnostic elements containing diagnostic information. The ValidateStateMachineDefinitionlAPI might add new diagnostics in the future, adjust diagnostic codes, or change the message wording. Your automated processes should only rely on the value of the result field…

definition.doc: The Amazon States Language definition of the state machine. For more information, see Amazon States Language (ASL).

type.doc: The target type of state machine for this definition. The default is STANDARD.

severity.doc: Minimum level of diagnostics to return. ERROR returns only ERROR diagnostics, whereas WARNING returns both WARNING and ERROR diagnostics. The default is ERROR.

maxResults.doc: The maximum number of diagnostics that are returned per call. The default and maximum value is 100. Setting the value to 0 will also use the default of 100. If the number of diagnostics returned in the response exceeds maxResults, the value of the truncated field in the response will be set to true.

result.doc: The result value will be OK when no syntax errors are found, or FAIL if the workflow definition does not pass verification.

diagnostics.doc: An array of diagnostic errors and warnings found during validation of the state machine definition. Since warnings do not prevent deploying your workflow definition, the result value could be OK even when warning diagnostics are present in the response.

truncated.doc: The result value will be true if the number of diagnostics found in the workflow definition exceeds maxResults. When all diagnostics results are returned, the value will be false.
